newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan repatriates 240 stowaways to rival China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan repatriates 240 stowaways to rival China.

text.p: Taiwan on Monday repatriated 240 Chinese illegal immigrants who sneaked into Taiwan to find work, but two mainland hijackers were not among the returnees, officials said on Monday.

"We have sent a total of 240...to Matsu. The mainland side will dispatch a ship from Mawei to pick these people up in neutral waters," a spokewoman for Taiwan's Hsinchu Mainlanders' Detention Centre told Reuters.
Matsu is a heavily fortified Taiwan-held defence outpost just 5.5 nautical miles from the Chinese mainland. Mawei is a mainland-held island nearby.
Taipei and Beijing have had no official contacts since a 1949 civil war split, but set an informal illegal immigrant repatration pact in 1990 through local Red Cross societies.
Repatriation nevertheless has been slow, especially since Beijing froze informal contacts in mid-1995.
Monday's repatriation leaves about 200 mainlanders awaiting return to the mainland, the last of 30,000 to pass through the island's three mainlander detention centres, officials said.
Hsinchu centre director Hu Yi-kang said Monday's handover did not include Chinese hijackers Huang Shukang and Han Fengying, though they have been approved for repatriation.
"They will be sent back separately," he said.
The two were among 16 mainlanders who hijacked jetliners to Taiwan in the early 1990s and were imprisoned for air piracy.
Huang and Han were released on parole in May but face deportation due to their undocumented status, and contacts about their repatration were under way, officials said.

Beijing in May returned Taiwan air pirate Liu Shan-chung -- completing the first cross-strait hijacker repatriation despite the two-year-old freeze on talks with Taiwan and the absence of a formal repatriation pact.
